chapter.title: The catflow wizard

section.title: Installation
section.para: Put the template (catflow.mxt) and helpfile (catflow.chm) into your ArcGIS template directory (C:\arcgis\arcexe83\bin\Templates).

If the directory differs, you'll need to adjust the path (public const helpfile) in the module CatflowUtil. To do this, start ArcMap with the catflow template. Go into the Visual Basic Editor (Extras:Macro:Visual Basic Editor...) and in the project frame open (Modles:CatflowUtil) where you can edit the corresponding path.
Copy the matlabScript folder to where you would like to run the matlab routines.

section.title: Starting the wizard
section.para:
In ArcMap, create a new file from the catflow template (File:New...). Select the catflow template from the register called general.
To start the wizard, click on the catflow toolbar.

section.title: Step 1: Introduction
section.para:
In the first step of the wizard, make sure the four shape files (the wizard does not work with coverages) as described in are available:
Digital Elevation Model
Vectorized river network
Slope delineation
Vectorized slope lines

section.title: Step 2: Rivernet file
section.para: In the second step you need to define the layer containing your vectorized river network. In , the layer is called riverNetWithAttrib. Two additional parameters for the river network are set during this step. The first is the default rivernet split length in meters. In the example, it is set to 20m. This defines at what interval river network points are created. These are then passed on to Catflow in a parameter file. The second parameter defines an attribute in the layer for specific split lengths. The attributes only define the river network point interval for a single river segment. If the entry in the attribute for a certain river stretch is negative, the default value (first parameter) is used instead.

example.title: Example clarifying what the priority of parameters is
example.para: While the following example describes priorities for the parameter river network split length equivalent priorities are used for all different parameters.

Let's assume your river network consists of three river segments with IDs 1,2, and 3. The specific rivernet split length attribute is set to SplitLength and the attribute table looks as follows:
ID SplitLenght
1 -1
2 -1
3 40
Moreover, your default split length is set to 20m. With these settings the split length is 20m for the river segements with ID 1 and 2 and it is 40m for the river segement with ID 3.

section.para: During step 2, also the layers with the digital elevation model (grid) and the rain station IDs (grid or polygon) need to be defined. Usually, the digital elevation model has only one attribute, otherwise the correct attribute (raster band) needs to be selected. The definition of the polygon theme with rain station IDs is optional. If a theme is defined, the rain station ID of a certain polygon will be assigned to the all rivernet points within this polygon. If a rivernet point does not fall within any polygon, a default ID (0) will be assigned. The information will then be passed on to Catflow.
If your river network theme contains the same line multiple times, you may get an error "more than one Outflow detected" while only one point shows up on the screen.

section.title: Step 3: Rivernet parameters
section.para: During the third step, all other rivernet parameters are defined. Since parameters for the river network are likely to differ with river size, default values for these parameters can be defined depending on the strahler order (). Besides the order-dependend default values, all parameters can also be assigned to river stretches with attributes. As described in , values in attribute fields are used If they are not negative. Non-negative values in attribute fields have higher priority than default values.

variablelist.title: River network parameters depending on strahler order

listitem.para: The critical rainfall m/s is used to estimate the river stretch geometry as described by p64

The width to depth ratio is an imporant parameter describing the river geometry. The width corresponds to the width of the river bed and the depth corresponds to the depth of the river for a flow corresponding to the critical rainfall. Used for calculations as described by p64.
Required to calculate the "Durchflussvermoegen"( p84). Unfortunately does not define the units. Is it the same as the Strickler-Beiwert as defined by p84 with units m1/3/s Called b_rauh in p.32
The channel bank slope 1/m defines the geometry of the channel bank. The bank rises 1m on a distance of m meters. Called b_m in p.32

Roads are often situated right next to the river. Water from these sealed surfaces reaches the river very fast. This parameter allows you to define the width of an area for which all of the rain reaches the river immediately p84. Called weg_br in p.32

varlistentry.term: Are sealed surfaces connected to the river?

listitem.para: See above. Called inarea in p.32

section.para: In the fourth step, layers defining the slope delineation and the vectorized slope lines are selected. In order to relate corresponding pairs of slope lines and polygons, both layers need unique IDs.

Step 5 can only be reached if a slope line exists for each polygon with the same ID. Note that slopes can not be processed if the slope line is not completely within the polygon theme. A warning will be issued if the slope line extends the corresponding polygon.
If the slope line goes crosses your river, an error ("object variable or with block variable not set") may occur. This will be corrected
section.title: Step 4: Slope files
Step 5: Slope parameters
section.para:
Step five allows to specify parameters for the two dimensional representation of the slopes. A two-dimensional grid based on curvlinear orthogonal coordinates is used. This has advantages for the numerical solution as described by p. 62 as well as flexible representation of the irregular boundery. The preprocessing allows to choose between two different representations of the slope. In the first case, all horizontal lines are parallel to the slope surface (constant thickness). In the second case, the bottom line is straight (cake shape).
"Cake-shaped" slope and slope with parallel lines (Source: Abb. 4.3, 4.4)
The thickness (extension along the z-coordinate) is defined at the bottom of the slope. The slope split length defines the spacing of points passed to the algorithm.

This algorithm is implemented in MATLAB making use of boundary descriptions by cubic splines. It allows to pass nothing than an arbitrary number of boundary points (in cartesian coordinates) to the algorithm instead of a mathematical description ( p.54).

Therefore it is best to define the split length a little larger than the horizontal resolution of the DEM. This way a maximum amount of information is passed to the algorithm while not introducing artefacts by repeated, equivalent altitudes (same DEM-cell).
As before, parameters can be defined as default as well as slope specific values in an attribute. Again, non-negative attributes override the default values.

The density of discretisation can be varied within the slope. It should be highest in areas expected to be hydrologically most active. The density is defined in terms of &eegr; and &xgr;, the curvlinear orthogonal coordinates.

Use the text fields to edit the list of coordinates. The list boxes show the parsed lists of coordinate points. &eegr; defines the horizontal coordinate with the maximum value corresponding to the bottom of the slope. &xgr; is the vertical coordinate with the maximum value representing the surface of the slope.
section.title: Step 6: Slope coordinates
Step 7: Finish
section.para: At this point, the wizard has all the information to produce two relevant output files. The first file, defined in the file dialog "Save Catflow rivernet data", can directly be used in Catflow as the river network geometry. The file format is described in p.31.

An error message (Iteration for depth is not stable after 500 steps. Using values as they are now. Check whether they are useful.) may occur during this last step. The wizard writes the files correctly. However, you should check whether river depths are meaningful values.
The second file, defined in the file dialog "Save slope data for Matlab preprocessing" needs to be processed by a Matlab program and will result in the hill slope geometries as described in p.34.

section.title: Matlab part of the preprocessing
section.para: Only one command needs to be executed in matlab. To do this, start matlab, change to your working directory (which contains h_spl.m and the other .m files) and type run h_spl.
A file dialog will open and allow you to select the data file created by the Catflow Wizard. The structure of the file is shown below.

variablelist.title: Structure of the slope data file created by the catflow wizard

listitem.para: numberOfSlopes (n), maxNumberOfSlopePoints (m), x_reference, y_reference, z_reference, number of &xgr; (i), number of &eegr; (j)
n columns with the slope IDs
n columns with the slope type (constant thickness (1) or 'Cake shape'(2))
n columns with the slope area
n columns with the number of points defining the slope surface
n columns with the thickness for each slope
m columns with x values for each slopepoint
m columns with y values for each slopepoint
m columns with z values for each slopepoint
m columns with width values for each slopepoint

section.para: After selecting the file, matlab will process each slope, generate a graph showing the slope profile and output the corresponding hillslope geometry (*.geo files) as defined in p.34.

chapter.section:
Program documentation
In order to understand the program documentation, you should be familiar with object oriented programming. First, an overview of the classes is given, then the classes are discussed in more detail. For documentation of ArcGIS-Standard classes, see the ArcGIS Deveoloper Help system distributed with ArcGIS.
The Catflow Wizard is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the .
Class overview
The wizard includes one form file and five classes. The form file provides the user interface and the classes are a representation of the geographical data and coresponding operations. shows the five classes. All functionality can be accessed through the two classes Slope and RiverNet. They create and handle the other objects (RiverSegment, RiverPoint and SlopePoint).
Classes used for the Catflow Wizard.
Wizard form
The wizard guides the user though the data generation. Its designed is based on a wizard tutorial at . The design is based on a Multipage Tabs object which shows the different registers subsequentially depending on the state of the program flow. The program flow control is event based. While the form is opened, the UserForm_Initialize-Method initializes lists and standard values and presents the intro page. The methods initialiseWithShapeLayers and initialiseWithRasterLayers are used to fill the lists containing GIS layers with names of corresponding laysers, while setupcbxDefaultGridShape is uesd to fill the list for the slope grid shape (compare )
The user navigates through the different registers using either the buttons or the subway map map (Left-hand side on the wizard, compare . These user actions call the methods

which are only active if the required previous steps are finished. These methods call the functions processRivernet and processSlopes if required while switching from one register to the next. These two functions are important becaues they create the shape files and objects for the subsequent program flow. During its execution processRivernet calls the method initializeStrahlerParameters and riverNetPointsIntoFeatureClass. InitializeStrahlerParameters is called at this point since the highest Strahler order is not known before the river network is processed, however this information is necessary for the setup of the interface of step 3. RiverNetPointsIntoFeatureClass adds the river network points into the corresponding shape file. This is supposed to be a functionality of the riverNet class, but it did not work within the riverNet object.
The state of the wizard is also changed if the user makes a selection in a list or combobox. These changes call one of the following methods. They set and reset internal variables according to the users selection and update the user interface if necessary by calling UpdateUI.

User actions include the three command buttons Cancel, Finish and Help which trigger the events

Cancel just unloads the form, while help opens the help file. Finish is only active if the required previous steps are finished. It then calls the three methods setDefaultsAndAttributeFields, showResults, and createCatflowFiles. SetDefaultsAndAttributeFields passes user input for default values and attribute field selections to the objects. showResults displays the newly created shape files, while createCatflowFiles generates the textfiles for catflow using the corresponding methods of the objects.
Slope Class
The Slope class provides the interface to convert GIS information into text files, which can be read by catflow after a further processing step with matlab (see also ).
Properties of the class Slope
Name Access Description Data Type Prerequisits
ID rw Unique ID. Generated as described in Integer
DEM rw The digital elevation model provides height information for the 2D representation of a slope. IFunctionalSurface
SlopeFallLine rw The slope fall line defines the line at which the 2D description of a slope is generated. IPath The slope fall line must be completely within the slope polygon.
SplitLength rw Distance between reference points used to describe the slope fall line Double
numberOfSlopePoints ro Number of reference points used to describe the slope fall line Integer Slope fall line and digital elevation model need to be set successfully before the number of reference points is available.
OutLet ro The outlet is the end point of the slope fall line. IPoint The slope fall line needs to be set successfully before the outlet is available
SlopePointFeatureClass rw A feature class (usually a shape file) which will hold the reference points used for the representation of the slope. IFeatureClass
SlopePolygon rw SlopePolygon describes the boundary of a slope. IPolygon The slope fall line must be completely within the slope polygon.
Area ro Area of the slope. Double SlopePolygon must be set.
ThiessenPolygon ro Thiessen polygons are used to calculate the width of the slope at a certain point. An error (errThiessenShapeVisible) is thrown if the shape file thiessenFeatureClass is visible. IPolygon The following properties must be set successfully before Thiessen polygons are available: thiessenFeatureClass, slopePointFeatureClass, DEM, and the slopeFallLine
ThiessenPolygonFeatureClass rw A feature class (usually a shape file) which will hold the Thiessen polygons used to calculate the width of the slope at a certain reference point.
IFeatureClass
Thickness rw Thickness (z-direction) of the slope at the bottom. Double
SlopeShapeType rw This property describes the shape of the slope. The two options are available as constants SlopeShapeTypeConstantThickness and SlopeShapeTypeCakeShape. Integer
XRef rw Reference value for the x coordinate. All other coordinates are reported with reference to this reference. Double
YRef rw Reference value for the y coordinate. All other coordinates are reported with reference to this reference. Double
ZRef rw Reference value for the z coordinate. All other coordinates are reported with reference to this reference. Double
The class offers the three methods updateThiessenFeatureClass, updatePointFeatureClass, and toMatlab. The first two methods update the content of the feature classes (shape files) based on the current properties of the class. toMatlab(w() As Double, X() As Double, Y() As Double, Z() As Double) returns the necessary coordinates (x,y,z, and width) as arrays to write the matlab input file.
The class also defines a few private functions and methods. The method splitFallLine generates equally spaced reference points as SlopePoint objects from the slope fall line. To do this, it uses the function addPoint(Point As IPoint) As SlopePoint, which creates a new SlopePoint object based on an IPoint object created during the split operation. The method deleteOld deletes all features from a feature class. This is necessary if properties of the slope are changed after points and Thiessen polygons are calculated. The method testSlopeLineWithinCatchment tests wheather a line is completely within a polygon, which is a required property for a slope fall line and a slope polygon. The function testSlopeLineToBeFlipped flippes slope lines based on the DEM if the outlet of the slope line is higher than the start point. The method reCalcSplit resets some internal flags (lineSplited, thiessenCalculated and slopePointFCisUpToDate) such that calculated properties are updated after relevant changes.
Slope Point Class
SlopePoint objects are used to represent the slope at all reference points. The advantage of using this class is, that SlopePoints provide the width of the slope at their position. To do that, they need to access some information of the corresponding slope object (e.g. thiessenPolygons, splitLength).
Properties of the class Slope
Name Access Description Data Type Prerequisits
Point rw The GIS-Object describing the coordinates of the slope point. IPoint The z-coordinate needs to be defined.
Slope rw The slope of which the SlopePoint is a part. Slope
Width ro The width of the slope at this point. Double Slope and Point need to be set.
X ro X-Coordinate of the point. Double The point needs to be set.
Y ro Y-Coordinate of the point. Double The point needs to be set.
Z ro Z-Coordinate of the point. Double The point needs to be set.
The class defines one private method calculateWidth which is called if the width needs to be recalculated. The width is calculated as the ratio of the area of the corresponding Thiessen polygon and the fall line length withing this polygon.
River Network Class
The RiverNetwork class provides the Interface to the functionality provided for river networks. Parameter properties of this class are set through common property methods, where the parameter type has to be specified. These can be any of the following integer values defined by the class: ParameterTypeSealedAreasConnected, ParameterTypeCriticalRain, ParameterTypeWidthToDepthRatio, ParameterTypeStrickler, ParameterTypeBankSlope, ParameterTypeSurfaceWidth, ParameterTypeSplitLength, and ParameterTypeRainStationID. See for a description of these parameters. If these parameters are defined in a field of the shape attribute table, this field can be defined either by name or by index number.
Properties of the class RiverNetwork
Name Access Description Data Type Prerequisits
RiverNetPoints ro Reference points for the parameterization of the river network. Multipoint The DEM and the Polylines need to be set first. However, this is not tested yet!
MaximumStrahlerOrder ro The Strahler order for the outflow river segment.
Long The DEM and the Polylines need to be set first. However, this is not tested yet!
DEM wo The digital elevation model for the area is important for the river geometry. IFunctionalSurface
Polylines rw This feature class (e.g. shape file) represents a collection of all relevant river segments. IFeatureClass DEM needs to be defined first. The shape type of the IFeatureClass needs to be polyline.
RainstationPolygons rw This feature class (e.g. shape file) contains polygons, which define the area for which the data of a certain rain station is relevant. IFeatureClass
topologySearchRadius rw If start and end points of adjacent river segments are not snaped, this radius defines the search radius within the next segment is searched. If the radius is set too large and multiple river segments have their start point within this radius, an error is thrown during the generation of the topology. Double
ParameterFieldIndex(parameterType As Long) rw Index number of the attribute field in the polyline feature class (shape file) containing values for the selected parameter type. Integer Polylines must be set in order to set the parameter field index.
ParameterFieldName(parameterType As Long) rw Name of the attribute field in the polyline feature class (shape file) containing values for the selected parameter type. String Polylines must be set in order to set the parameter field index.
DefaultParameterValue(parameterType As Long, Optional StrahlerOrder As Integer = -1) rw Default value for a certain parameter This value is overriden by entries in the corresponding parameter field (if one is defined). Some parameters depend on the strahler order and are only accessable, if the StrahlerOrder is passed during the call. Double The default value must be within the valid range
The class defines the following three methods and functions: connectSlope(s As slope) allows to connect a slope object to the nearest reference point of the river network. If another slope is connected to the same reference point, an error occurs. toCatflow(outStream As TextStream) writes all catflow specific parameters to outStream. The function getRainstationID(Point As IPoint) returns the ID for the relevant rain station for a certain point. If the point is outside the defined polygons, the default value is returned.
Internally, the class uses a number of private functions and methods. The function numberOfUpStreams returns the number of upstream segments for a certain segment. The function numOfOutflows returns the number of out flows for a river network. This should be one for a network with a correct topology.
The processing of the river network is done mainly by two methods: The first method extractPathpolylines generates river segments from the polyline feature class. After counting the number of polylines, all arrays are initialized with the method initializeArrays. Parameter values are assigned to all RiverSegment objects and all segments are tested whether they are pointing in a downstream direction with the method findReversedPolylines. Then the topology is created with the method calcTopology. An error with the number errorTooManyOutflows occurs if more than one outflows are counted, which means that some river segments are not connected to the rest of the river network.
The second method for the processing of the river network is called calcExecutionSequence and assigns parameters and sequence numbers (increasing from springs to the outlet) for all reference points of the river network. First, all springs are added to a queue with the method allSpringsToQueue. The method processNextSegment handels the actual processing of a river segment (i.e. assigning sequence numbers, calculationg Strahler order ( setStrahlerOrderNextDownstream), and marking segment as processed). Also each processed river segment adds the next downstream segment "A" to the queue if there are no more unprocessed segments upstream of A. This way, it is assured that for each segment all upstream segments have lower sequence numbers.
The method pathIsReversed reverses the orientation of the segment within the method findReversedPolylines. The methods showPath and showOutflows are used to indicate topological errors of the river network during execution of the method calcTopology. The method reinitializeRiverNet resets some internal flags in order to restart calculations after a change of properties. The method Class_Initialize finally initialized the array for the default values.
Improvements for next version (ToDo):
Calling reinitializeRiverNet always if necessary and check whether required properties are set before calculations are started (fail-prove).
Since Strahler order is required to assign parameters correctly and parameters are assigned during the same step as the order is calculated, this step is called twice. However, this can be omitted if the river segment class does not have its copies of all properties (see below)

The RiverSegment class provides the function assignNumbers(start As Integer, lastRiverPoint() As RiverPoint). Parameters are the lowest river point ID to be used (start) as well as an array of the previous RiverPoints upstream of the current segment (lastRiverPoint). The return value is the highest river point ID used. The method connectSlope(s As slope, PointID As Integer) allows to assign the slope s to the RiverPoint with the identification PointID. This means that the water leaving slope s will enter the river network at this point. The method toCatflow(outStream As TextStream) writes the parameters for the RiverSegment to the specified text stream.
The class also defines to internal methods. addPoint creates new RiverPoint objects from ArcGIS IPoint objects and assigns correct ID numbers and topology information. The method testPointAvailability is called if properties are queried which require that identification numbers have been assigned. If this hasn't been done, then IDs are assigned starting from 0. If the path property has not been set, the method will raise an error.
Improvements for the next version: Change the class such that the RiverSegment object does not know it's physical properties (). If these are required, it will query them from the corresponding RiverNet object. This allows a slimmer object interface. It also solves the problem of calling the parameter assignement method twice (see improvements for the rivernet class).
How about removing this class entirely? Creating the correct river points could be done by the RiverNet object. All other calls are (more or less?) passed to the collection of all river points.
River Point Class
The RiverPoint object defines a reference point in the river network for which physical properties are known (or computed). Properties of the class RiverPoint
Name Access Description Data Type Prerequisits
River net rw River net of which the point is a part of. RiverNet
X rw The x-coordinate of the river point Double
Y rw The y-coordinate of the river point Double
Z rw The z-coordinate of the river point Double
IPoint ro The ArcGIS object describing all coordinates of the river point IPoint
ID rw The identification (sequence) number of the river point Integer
order rw The order of the river point Double

upStreamCount ro The number of river point objects directly upstream (Without other river point objects inbetween the current and the listed river point) of the current point. This can be greater than 1 because of tributaries. Integer
UpstreamRiverPoint(position As Integer) ro The river point object directly upstream. Since it is possible to have muliple such points, the position in the list of all upstream river point objects needs to be specified. Can be set through two methods (see the text below the table). RiverPoint Position must be valid, i.e. >0 and ⪕upStreamCount
RiverSegment rw The river segment of which the point is a part of RiverSegment
IsTheOutlet rw True for the most downstream river point of the catchment Boolean
ChannelDepth rw Depth of the channel at this position. Can be assigned or is estimated (through iteration) from physical parameters. Double prereq

ChannelBottomElevation ro
Elevation of the channel bottom = (DEM-elevation at this point) - (channel depth)
If the depth has not been estimated before, this triggers the iteration. Since the channel bottom elevation of neighboring river points is required for the estimation formula, an infinite series of method calls would occur, if this method was used by the estimation formula. See also the next property. Double
currentChannelBottomElevation ro The current estimation of the elevation based on the current value for the depth. Double
ChannelBottomSlope ro The slope at the bottom of the channel at the river point. Double
ChannelBottomWidth ro The width at the bottom of the channel at the river point. Double
Slope rw Slope object assigned to this river point or nothing. The corresponding slope discharges into the river at this point. Slope
slopeID ro ID of the assigned slope or 0 Integer
SlopeArea ro Area of the assigned slope or 0 Double
CatchmentArea ro Area of the catchment for the river point Double
A method and a function allow to manipulate upstream river points: The function deleteUpstreamRiverPoint(RiverPoint As RiverPoint) removes the specified river point from the list of upstream river points. Returns true upon successfull deletion. The method AddUpstreamRiverPoint(RiverPoint As RiverPoint) adds the specified point to the list of upstream river points.
Four functions and two method are used internally for the estimation of the river depth. The iteration is started with the private method estimateDepth. From this method, the function iterationStep is called until it returns true (iteration is stable for all river points) or until the upper limit of iteration staeps is reached. In the later case, the allDepthsOK sets the depthIsOK-flag for all river points, supressing further estimation. A warning is issued in this case. The slope at the channel bottom is required to estimate the depth. It is calculated with the private function calcChannelBottomSlope(iterating As Boolean). If the parameter is true, the property currentChannelBottomElevation from neighboring points is used in order to avoid a second triggering of the iteration. The estimation formula for the depth is defined in the private function depthEstimationFormula. The method allDepthsOutput allows to output the current values for all river points for debuging purposes.
The class defines two additional methods. CatflowParameterOutput writes a line with all required parameters for catflow to the specified stream. The private method Class_Initialize initializes some of the internal variables.
Improvements for the next version: Improve iteration. In some cases, it is numerical instable, e.g. some river points alternate between two values at the end. The property DepthIterationLimit might be more appropriate at the level of the riverNet.
